subject.title: [Bug]: Agent / sessions_spawn tool_use can emit with no matching tool_result and no parent-visible signal — silent subagent drop (~3.8% historical rate)

question: Should OpenClaw standardize failed subagent completion as a synthetic tool_result, a durable queued session/task event, or a combined contract that both wakes the parent and closes the result pairing?
rationale: The code has multiple partial recovery surfaces, and choosing the model-visible contract affects transcript shape, provider compatibility, retries, task delivery, and user-facing channel behavior.

options.title: Combined Durable Result Contract
options.body: Create a durable parent-visible failure event that also closes the outstanding subagent result pairing, then make timeout, no-output, and give-up paths converge on it.

options.title: Task Wake First
options.body: Land the narrow requester-wake PR first and leave synthetic tool_result semantics for a follow-up design issue.

options.title: Synthetic Result Only
options.body: Inject a typed error result in transcript paths without changing task delivery, which is narrower but may not solve busy-requester durable delivery loss.

recommendation.title: Combined Durable Result Contract
recommendation.body: Create a durable parent-visible failure event that also closes the outstanding subagent result pairing, then make timeout, no-output, and give-up paths converge on it.

likelyOwner.reason: The current recovery slice relies on task registry and delivery-policy seams where this history is strongest.
